[01:26.0] I was called to serve on the NIWRC board by some of the aunties that have been in the organization
[01:31.4] for anywhere between 10 to 12 years.
[01:34.0] I have been running the Idaho Coalition Against Sexual and Domestic Violence since 2019,
[01:41.0] so it was an opportunity to step into leadership that was specifically engaging native women and girls,
[01:47.0] and that was appealing to me because I am a native woman and was once a native girl.
[01:51.0] I'm also a descendant of women who've experienced violence in my community,
[01:56.0] and when I showed up to my first meeting, we were in Arizona,
[01:59.0] and I wasn't expecting to take on a leadership role, but was asked to take on leadership
[02:05.0] because of how politically and policy driven that I've been in state coalition spaces,

[03:01.8] I think in our communities, we really try to work in such a way where the future generations

[04:07.1] Oh my goodness, there's so many changes that we can celebrate across the country from the work of NIWRC.
[04:14.1] I'm thinking about policy changes that we've made, how much the shift that the Office of Violence Against Women
[04:22.1] has made in supporting Native communities in the way that we do this work.
[04:25.1] The expansion into Alaska and Hawaii are big changes as well.
[04:30.1] And I also think that the very intentional inclusion of Native women in Congress, both federally and at the state level,
[04:38.1] our voices as Native women in national initiatives around safety and wellness is also indicative of the fact that
[04:45.1] we've made some sweeping revolutionary changes in just our generation.
[05:00.0] NIWRC is Native women-led for a number of reasons, and I think that our deep cultural alignment to nature and to land
[05:09.6] is a good reason why we energize that sort of leadership.
[05:13.0] A lot of our nations, we believe that water is life-giving as women are life-giving, that Earth and nature is life-giving as women are

[06:44.7] And I think that, you know, I think that for the future, and I think that for our communities in general,

[07:07.2] because it wouldn't be that way in a system that's not designed to involve us.
[07:20.7] Yes, yes. [do not use: intro or crew talk]
